I don't have a problem with this because, quite frankly, a lot of people in TN haven't been exposed to this type of information since the state is so conservative. The school wasn't funding it, merely accommodating the events. Cue the crazy assault on the school led primarily by a lunatic named Stacey Campfield...a carpet-bagger tea-party activist who got elected to be a state rep from Knoxville. He, and others of his ilk just went nuts about Sex Week and made it a big issue which in turn made TN out to be a bunch of backwoods Hillbillies. He was thrown out of office last year, but is now a delegate for Trump.

This campaign by Campfield effectively politicized the University of Tennessee and put it under the state legislature's microscope. TN is a 1-party state, with conservative Republicans having a super-majority so they pander to any crazy, right-wing outrage du-jour.

The UT Diversity office is staffed by--wait for it--crazy SJWs who do what SJWs normally do...say stupid shit. In this case, they sent out some internal emails reminding folks that "Christmas" parties in December might be construed as exclusionary to non-Christians. But then, they upped their stupidity and sent out an email encouraging the use of gender-neutral pronouns and telling faculty that they should query EVERY student about their preferred pronouns. Now this is just patently stupid, and in a conservative state like TN it was red-meat to the state legislature just looking for another reason to attack. This pretty much coincided with the recent UM and Harvard nonsense so it got a lot of play. The dude (African American) who is the head of the UT Diversity office is now interviewing at a couple of other (non TN) schools. Ultimately, the legislature backed off the threats of cuts (reducing them to less than 500,000) primarily because the billionaire governor (Haslam-R) talked some sense into them about how it might affect Title IX Federal Funding...of course this is an entirely separate conversation.

I'm all for calling out stupid SJW bullshit and I think it's appropriate that the UT administration has been put on notice, however I remain concerned that the Republicans in the state have also effectively threatened to punish the school over allowing the students to have Sex Week, which I consider well within their free-speech rights since it is student-funded and run.
